root_idea.summary: A root centered on nearness, the opposite of distance: being close in place, time, relation, rank, access, or degree.
root_idea.development: The lexical field extends from physical approach and proximity to temporal imminence, kinship, favored status, seeking nearness to God, offerings made for that purpose, and specialized uses involving approach to water, approximation, and containment.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Inflected plural of the separately attested Quranic noun قُرْبَة; represented under its singular dictionary headword.

senses.definition: To approach, come near, or be close to something.
senses.usage_conditions: Used for physical proximity and approach; the Quranic imperfect forms occur especially in prohibitions against approaching a person, place, object, or act.

senses.definition: To approach or engage in an act or object; in the construction قَرِبَ المرأةَ, to have sexual intercourse by euphemism.
senses.usage_conditions: In prohibitive constructions, the wording can prohibit not only the final act but also approaching or engaging in what leads to it. لا تَقْرَبُوهُنَّ is an established euphemism for sexual intercourse, while لا تَقْرَبُوا الزِّنَى prohibits approaching or engaging in fornication.

senses.definition: To cause to be near; to bring or draw someone or something close.
senses.usage_conditions: Transitive causative use, including bringing a person near or placing an object near someone.

senses.definition: To bring near in standing, favor, access, or rank.
senses.usage_conditions: The object is brought near figuratively, as an associate, favored person, or one granted proximity to God or a ruler.

senses.definition: To present, offer, or place something before someone, especially as an offering.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction قَرَّبَهُ إِلَيْهِمْ, the object is presented or placed before the recipients; the related offering construction includes presenting a قربان.

senses.definition: To draw near, come near, or become imminent.
senses.usage_conditions: Used for an approaching event or time as well as ordinary coming near; the form can convey intensified or completed approach.

senses.definition: To draw near to God through worship or submission.
senses.usage_conditions: The imperative وَاقْتَرِب is a religious construction of drawing near, not a claim of bodily movement toward God.

senses.definition: Nearer or nearest; closer in place, time, degree, or standing.
senses.usage_conditions: Comparative or superlative adjective, sometimes substantivized; the comparison may concern physical distance, appropriateness, or rank.

senses.definition: A nearer or closest relative; near kin.
senses.usage_conditions: Substantivized plural forms refer to relatives or kindred, with nearness understood in kinship rather than physical distance.
A relational noun describing someone connected by close kinship.

senses.definition: Brought near, admitted to favor, or granted honored proximity, especially to God.
senses.usage_conditions: Passive participle of قَرَّبَ; in Quranic contexts it denotes persons granted a privileged spiritual rank or nearness, not merely physical proximity.
Describes spatial proximity; the adjective may retain the masculine form with a conventionally feminine subject in some Quranic and Classical constructions.

senses.definition: Near in time; imminent, soon, or after a short interval.
senses.usage_conditions: Used of future or past time and may be translated “soon,” “shortly,” or “impending” according to context.

senses.definition: Near in care, response, or accessible presence.
senses.usage_conditions: In descriptions of God or divine mercy, nearness is relational and spiritual—expressing care, response, or availability rather than bodily location.

senses.definition: An offering presented for nearness to God; by conventional extension, a sacrifice.
senses.usage_conditions: Includes a sacrificial offering and, more broadly, anything presented as an act of seeking divine nearness.
A relational noun referring to close family connection or those connected by kinship; it can also denote the relationship itself.

senses.definition: A means or act of seeking nearness to God.
senses.usage_conditions: Includes a righteous deed, prayer, offering, or other act intended to gain divine favor or proximity; the plural قُرُبَات refers to such means or acts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To form an opinion approaching certainty.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of nearness applied to judgment or estimation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become near to setting.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare usage in which the ق is reported as a substitute for ك in the corresponding verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To journey toward water by night in order to reach it soon, especially on the following morning.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized pastoral term concerning a person or group traveling with camels toward a watering place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person seeking or journeying toward water, especially by night.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may be restricted to nighttime water-seeking according to some authorities.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek, aim at, or undertake the accomplishment of an affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension from journeying toward a sought destination or water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Drawing near or causing proximity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal noun and derived usage associated with approach and nearness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The sheath, scabbard, or carrying case of a sword or knife.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May refer narrowly to the scabbard or more broadly to a case containing the weapon and related equipment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Near a specified time.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used adverbially, as in arriving near nightfall or near the night.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Nearly equal or nearly equivalent in quantity or amount.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of an amount that nearly fills, matches, or equals a stated quantity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The flank or side of the body, especially the region from the side to the soft parts of the belly or armpit.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Especially used of an animal, particularly a horse; the plural أَقْرَاب can also occur in a culinary expression for feeding a guest with flanks.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Nearness or vicinity in place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used as a substantive or adverbial expression for being within a short distance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Nearness in time; soon.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A temporal use distinct from spatial vicinity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Nearness of station, grade, rank, or favor.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of admission into another’s favor or of a privileged position, apart from the specifically devotional sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A skin or leather vessel used for carrying water or milk.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A container made from an animal skin, with several established plural forms.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A quantity in a vessel that nearly fills it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression فِيهِ قَرَبَةٌ of a vessel nearly filled.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A vessel that is nearly full.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A distinct nominal use, unrelated to the offering noun قُرْبَان.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A favored, intimate, or special associate or companion, especially of a ruler or other person of authority.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A person is called this because of privileged nearness or admission into favor.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be nearly full, nearly equal, or nearly equivalent to a stated amount.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a vessel approaching fullness or of an amount approaching another amount.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make steps, words, or events close together or nearly continuous.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applies to shortened steps, rapidly delivered speech, closely spaced words, or nearly uninterrupted affairs.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To consider someone or something near or nearly so.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A cognitive use involving estimation rather than actual physical proximity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To exchange good or pleasing speech with someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional interpersonal use of the Form III verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pursue a moderate, right, or just course, neither exceeding nor falling short.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of conduct in an affair, including fair dealing in buying or selling.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sexual approach or intercourse-related act.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized expression involving raising the leg for sexual intercourse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be near giving birth or bringing forth young.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a pregnant woman or female animal; the evidence lists mares, ewes, goats, and asses, with differing remarks about camels.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To approach the age at which an animal sheds its central or other teeth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used especially of a colt or young camel.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To perform something nearly equal or similar to a specified model.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested in the expression for performing a prayer nearly like the Prophet’s prayer.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Advance, come forward, or hasten.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The evidence specifically identifies the imperative as the form used in this sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To draw oneself near, ally oneself, ingratiate oneself, or seek access and favor.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May describe approach through affection, friendship, a performed act, or righteous action; it can also be used of seeking nearness to God.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To place one’s hand on one’s flank while walking or hastening.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized bodily description of movement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To draw near to one another or become close together.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reciprocal or collective Form VI use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become few, reduced, or diminished.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of camels and, by extension, other things that become fewer or deteriorate.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become nearly ripe.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of seed produce, standing corn, or similar crops.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become contracted or shortened in duration.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative temporal extension of becoming close together.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To reckon something remote as near or regard it as close.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The opposite of اِسْتَبْعَدَ in the cited construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A relation or relative by birth or marriage.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In this relational use the adjective is substantivized and takes ordinary feminine, dual, and plural forms.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Near or allied through affection, friendship, or cordiality.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A social and emotional use rather than spatial proximity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Near in quality, likeness, learning, or degree.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in comparisons such as being near to the likeness or competence of another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Salted fish while still fresh and moist.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare nominal use with variant pronunciation reported in the lexicons.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Relationship or kinship, including relationship through the womb or female side.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A relational noun whose precise scope may distinguish general lineage from uterine or maternal kinship.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A believer’s intuitive insight or an opinion approaching knowledge and assurance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized expression describing spiritual discernment or inspired perception.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Near together or close to one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression جَاؤُوا قُرَابَى of people arriving close together.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A maker of water skins or related leather containers.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An occupational noun derived from the water-skin sense of the root.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small boat, skiff, or ship’s boat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nautical noun, distinct from the water-seeker use of قَارِب.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Water so copious that one cannot cope with or master it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal description of overpowering water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Foretokens that water is near, such as small pebbles encountered by a well-digger.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical plural expression concerning signs that a spring is close beneath the ground.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A near or nearest road, path, or approach; sometimes a small way leading into a larger one.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can also denote a conspicuous road or a place of alighting or encampment according to the cited authorities.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A horse kept close at hand and prepared for riding or running; by extension, a saddled or prepared camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Descriptions vary between a generously treated horse kept near the dwelling, a horse prepared by restricted feeding, and mounts equipped for riding.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Middling, ordinary, inexpensive, or not of high quality.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a person, garment, commodity, religion, or other thing that falls between good and bad or is cheap rather than precious.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A short person whose extremities are close together.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A bodily description derived from the idea of parts being near one another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The Arabic poetic meter al-Mutaqārib.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical prosodic term, so called because its metrical feet or pegs are close together.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To offer a visitor welcome by wishing that his dwelling be made near or convenient.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Part of the greeting حَيَّاكَ اللهُ وَقَرَّبَ دَارَكَ addressed to a guest.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Presenting an argument so that the desired conclusion follows necessarily.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical use of the verbal noun in reasoning and proof.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A particular running gait of a horse, between ordinary trotting and full gallop.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The gait involves raising and setting down the forelegs together; two grades, a higher and lower type, are reported.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The verbal-noun use denoting nearness is covered by the causative nearness sense.
Nearness to a person or thing is the same general semantic branch as approach and proximity.
The buying and selling example is a specific application of pursuing a moderate or just course.
The group’s camel-driving state is covered by the specialized journey-to-water meaning.
Pointer-only cross-reference to the Form I discussion.
A specific formulation of the journey-to-water meaning.
A direct example of the relational adjective.
A diminutive and proverbially specific expression within the kinship branch.
Pointer to another root article; no lexical meaning is stated here.
The direct comparative and superlative meaning is represented by the Quranic adjective entry.
The active-participle form expresses the same near-birth specialization as the verb.
Orthographic/editorial correction identifying the form as a likely error for a different root.

cautions: The normalized public headword قَرُبَ represents the QAC Form I imperfect group whose attested surface forms are تَقْرَبَ, تَقْرَبُ, and يَقْرَبُ.
In descriptions of God or divine mercy, Quranic nearness is relational, spiritual, or expressive of care and response, not bodily location.
قَرِيب may retain a masculine form with a conventionally feminine subject in some Classical constructions, including the Quranic expression concerning divine mercy.
The plural Quranic group قُرُبَٰت is presented under the singular citation form قُرْبَة because the packet separately attests the singular and the plural has the same devotional meaning.
